record_type_quote: On this basis, the first aim of the current study was to attempt a direct replication of Kallitsounaki and Williams’ (2020) recently published findings of the relations between autistic traits, gender dysphoric feelings, recalled cross-gender behaviour, and mentalising ability in a new sample of adults from the general population to increase confidence in the veracity of the original findings.

targets.title: Mentalising moderates the link between autism traits and current gender dysphoric features in primarily non-autistic, cisgender individuals.
targets.evidence_quote: On this basis, the first aim of the current study was to attempt a direct replication of Kallitsounaki and Williams’ (2020) recently published findings of the relations between autistic traits, gender dysphoric feelings, recalled cross-gender behaviour, and mentalising ability in a new sample of adults from the general population to increase confidence in the veracity of the original findings.
targets.outcome_quote: In sum, the current study successfully reproduced (a) the link between autistic traits and current gender dysphoric feelings/recalled cross-gender behaviour and (b) the relation between mentalising and current gender dysphoric feelings, reported by Kallitsounaki and Williams (2020).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly summarize the targeted replication as successful. Additional mediation findings extend the original; the original non-significant autistic traits/mentalising association is discussed in the extension.

reasoning: Full primary article acquired including reference list. Title, all three authors and DOI match. One target paper; other cited gender/autism findings are background. Explicit overall verdict governs outcome.
